page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the c8i.8xlarge demonstrates strong performance in several areas. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2187.0 and a multi-core score of 18229.0, both falling into the strong category. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 34.25 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 227.98 GB/sec. For LLM inference using a small 135M model, text generation reaches a top-tier speed of 357.67 tokens/sec, while prompt processing for a medium 7B model registers at 202.5 tokens/sec. Passmark CPU encryption and physics tests also rank in the strong tier.

The hardware profile presents specific tradeoffs. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external network storage, and the baseline network bandwidth is limited to 15 Gbps. The 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases, though its DDR5 memory speed of 7 GHz helps maintain an average memory read-only large block bandwidth of 178.37 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated Intel Xeon cores and advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and AMX, provide high compute density for vector and matrix operations without the overhead of a GPU.

This instance is configured for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and advanced instruction sets. Suitable applications include software compilation, image processing, text processing, static web serving, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference tasks.
